ny_ice_pond.blurb: Ice Pond is a boulder-only area in Putnam County, New York, near Brewster Hill and Patterson, close to Route 84. The boulders are glacial leftovers, dropped by melting ice many thousands of years ago, and the rock is gneiss. Problems cover the whole range from V0 up to V10, with a couple of V12s, and the middle grades are well stocked, including a solid run of V6 to V9. Moby Area holds the most climbs, followed by Diesel and Ice Cube Area and Mercury Area, while Sloper City is a small cluster of just a few problems. Side trails branch off the main path to reach different boulder fields.

or_trout_creek.blurb: Trout Creek is a crack-climbing crag in north-central Oregon, near Madras and the lower Deschutes River. The rock is rough basalt in big columns, and the climbing is almost entirely gear-protected: vertical cracks in corners and stemboxes, in a place with a tradition of not adding new bolts. Most routes fall between 5.10 and 5.12, with a growing number of 5.13s and a few easier, lower-angle cracks on the north side. The Main Wall holds the most climbs and faces west, which sets when it gets sun and when it is in shade. The Northern End and the Cool Wall are smaller sections.

wa_ozone.blurb: Ozone is a cliff band on the Washington side of the Columbia Gorge, on the south side of Highway 14 outside Washougal, reached by a narrow trail through fir forest. The cliff stretches roughly 800 feet and is split into eleven sections, many with Middle-earth names. It holds both trad and sport routes. Most grades fall between 5.8 and 5.11, with a few easier lines and a handful of 5.12s. The first section at the west end is about 40 feet tall, and the rock gets taller toward the center. Many of the moderate routes sit in shade. Old School Wall holds the most climbs, followed by Heaven's Wall and Mordor.

wy_pinedale_area.blurb: The Pinedale Area gathers the scattered climbing around Pinedale, Wyoming. It is mostly bouldering, with a smaller number of trad and sport routes and a couple of top-ropes. Boulder problems run from V0 to V8 with the bulk in the easy to middle grades, and the roped climbs mostly fall between 5.8 and 5.10, with a few at 5.11. The rock is mostly granite. Winter typically arrives in late October and holds until May, so the climbing season is short. Stonehenge holds the most climbs: a field of granite boulders of all sizes south of Pinedale near Boulder, with bolted routes on the taller rock, where summer is the suggested time for bouldering and sport. Soda/Willow Lake Road and Halfmoon Lake come next.

ca_b_el_capitan.blurb: El Capitan is the granite wall on the north side of Yosemite Valley, near its western end, rising roughly 3,000 feet. Two main faces, the Southwest and the Southeast, meet at a prow. The rock is pale, coarse-grained granite. This is big wall terrain: long multi-pitch trad and aid lines, with only a few sport routes and boulder problems. Free grades mostly run from 5.8 to 5.11, with a smaller group of 5.12 to 5.14, alongside a set of aid-graded lines. Base Routes holds the most climbs, followed by the Southwest Face and the Southeast Face, while the East Buttress is a single line.
